question: Which of the following rules can be used to determine the direction of magnetic field due to a current carrying circular loop?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right Hand Thumb Rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right Hand Thumb Rule**, also known as **Maxwell’s Corkscrew Rule**, is a fundamental principle used to determine the direction of the **magnetic field** associated with a **current-carrying conductor**, including a **circular loop**.
 
• According to this rule, if you imagine holding the current-carrying wire in your **right hand** such that your **thumb** points in the direction of the **electric current**, then your **curled fingers** will point in the direction of the **magnetic field lines**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• In the case of a **circular loop**, the magnetic field lines near the wire are in the form of **concentric circles**. As we move towards the **center of the loop**, the arcs of these big circles appear as **straight lines**.
 
• Every section of the wire contributes to the magnetic field lines in the same direction within the loop. At the **center of the circular loop**, the magnetic field is **perpendicular** to the plane of the loop.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying wire at a given point depends directly on the **magnitude of the current (I)** passing through it and inversely on the **distance (r)** from the wire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fleming’s Left Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is primarily used to find the direction of the **magnetic force** acting on a moving **charge** or a **current-carrying conductor** placed in an external **magnetic field**.
 
• It is commonly applied in the working of an **electric motor**.
 
• The **forefinger** represents the **field**, the **middle finger** represents the **current**, and the **thumb** represents the **motion or force**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fleming’s Right Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of the **induced current** when a conductor moves inside a **magnetic field**.
 
• It is the basis for the operation of an **electric generator**.
 
• The **thumb** shows the **direction of motion**, the **forefinger** shows the **field**, and the **middle finger** shows the direction of the **induced current**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Maxwell’s Left Hand Rule:**
 
 
• There is no widely recognized "Maxwell's Left Hand Rule" in standard electromagnetism for determining field directions. James Clerk Maxwell is specifically associated with the **Right-Hand Corkscrew Rule**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Clock-Face Rule:** A simple method to find the **polarity** of a **circular loop**. If the current flows in an **anti-clockwise** direction, the face of the loop behaves like a **North Pole**. If the current flows in a **clockwise** direction, the face behaves like a **South Pole**.
 
• **Number of Turns:** If there is a circular coil having **n turns**, the field produced is **n times** as large as that produced by a single turn. This is because the current in each circular turn has the same direction, and the field due to each turn then just adds up.
 
• **Magnetic Field Formula:** For a circular loop of **radius R** carrying **current I**, the magnetic field **(B)** at the center is given by **B = (μ₀I) / (2R)**, where **μ₀** is the **permeability of free space**.
